quarterly_data.quarter: CoreWeave press release: CoreWeave Delivers NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Performance at (09-30-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CoreWeave announced the availability of NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 on CoreWeave, with Cognition (the applied AI lab behind Devin) as what CoreWeave calls the first customer anywhere running production workloads on the system; Cognition worked with CoreWeave to stand up a Vera Rubin NVL72 cluster in early September. Customers run the system under the same operating model and tooling as their existing NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 and GB300 NVL72 fleets. In Cognition's own benchmarks on CoreWeave Cloud, Vera Rubin NVL72 delivered a 4.8 times increase in total token throughput for its SWE-2 inference workloads versus a GB200 NVL72 baseline and a 3.8 times boost in output token throughput for reinforcement learning workloads. CoreWeave says it has published measured silicon performance on the platform showing 10 times the token throughput per megawatt over NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 on the DeepSeek R1 reasoning model at matched interactivity. Cognition scaled from bridge capacity to thousands of GPUs for training and inference on CoreWeave in less than nine months. EVP Chen Goldberg: having a customer 'already seeing performance gains within days' is the payoff from years of engineering across GPU generations. The release adds that NVIDIA Volta GPUs (relationship with NVIDIA dating to 2017) are still in commercial service on CoreWeave Cloud.
quarterly_data.figure: Vera Rubin NVL72 available; 4.8 times total token throughput (SWE-2 inference) and 3.8 times output token throughput (RL) vs GB200 NVL72; 10 times token throughput per megawatt on DeepSeek R1; cluster stood up in early September
